Second run of the skill, and the first where it existed BEFORE the work. What it taught:

WHAT HELD. The milestone commits worked exactly as intended -- six commits, each independently green, and the one time I needed to fix something mid-flight (the dedup bug) it landed as its own commit without disturbing the rest. 'Fix, don't report' held under pressure: four translator gaps found, three fixed, one deferred with a reason.

The skill should say: look for a metric that reads implausibly across existing projects, not only for a construct nobody has.

WHAT THE USER CAUGHT THAT THE SKILL DID NOT. Asked whether the recommendation generalised. It did not -- I had designed an sh_test mapping from jansson alone, and surveying six projects showed TESTS has three shapes with jansson in the MINORITY (gsl alone has 54 binaries run directly). The skill needs an explicit rule: before building a capability from one project's shape, measure the shape across 5+ projects. That single question changed the design from a mapping to a classifier.

ALSO: the 'must ship configure' selection rule was overstated (bzl-mu5), corrected mid-run after the user challenged it.

THE TWO-PILE SPLIT held up but needed a third state. bzl-lno.4 (@var@ in prose) is neither agent work nor a translator gap worth fixing -- it is an accepted cost, recorded. The skill's binary framing has no slot for that.
